Entity, permission and MFA hardcoding audit

3 October 2026 · Asia/Kuala_Lumpur · Current working tree

2,993 files scanned; 712 files flagged; 213 application-source candidates.

Counts identify static review candidates, not confirmed defects. Categories overlap. Tests, generic IAM enforcement and model-schema strings need different treatment from entity-specific runtime dispatch. No application code, MFA code, database grants or deployments changed during this audit.

Permission literals/templates: 297 files overall, 90 application files. MFA literals/configuration: 90 overall, 28 application files. Broader counts also include permission-presence review checks and MFA identifier references.

Important status

  • The workforce entity allowlist and derived permissions introduced by this assistant remain an architectural defect.
  • Four unfinished MFA-related source changes remain pending after the stop instruction; this audit did not approve, finish or revert them.
  • The new absent-permission rule requires a coordinated schema/compiler/runtime design. Current parser, read, mutation and action paths still assume permissions exist.
  • Existing platform-control MFA and generic requirement-driven IAM checks must not be removed based on a keyword count.

Manually reviewed findings

38 findings across 36 files, including 19 files with confirmed concrete entity/permission hardcoding. This is a reviewed lower bound, not the total number of violations.
